transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
International climate change negotiations in Turkey broke down in the final hours today
over fossil fuels, and Piers Lauren Sommer has more.
The key sticking point was over fossil fuels.
Countries were negotiating an agreement to move away from using energy like coal and
natural gas, which produced heat-trapping emissions that warmed the planet.
Countries like Saudi Arabia rejected that language, leading the European Union and others
to walk out.
The U.S. was not at the negotiations.
Fossil fuels were part of a climate deal agreed to back in 2023.
Now, some countries are questioning the value of the United Nations climate talks.
Most countries are not on track to meet their pledges to cut emissions.
Lauren Sommer, NPR News.
The Justice Department has told a court that the U.S. Army will detonate close to five
tons of bomb-making material containing lead at a site in Iowa by Tuesday.
And Piers Andrea Shue reports that's despite a court order pausing the detonation.
At issue are 68 drums of what the U.S. Army says is significantly degraded and unstable
lead azide at a facility in Middletown, Iowa.
The Army has argued that because the material is at risk of exploding simultaneously, a
planned explosion would be safer.
It had planned to detonate the material on Friday, a week after the EPA granted the Army
an emergency permit.
But two environmental groups sued to block that permit, citing irreparable health and
environmental harm and failure by the EPA to properly evaluate alternatives.
Last week, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals temporarily suspended the permit.
Now, the Justice Department is arguing the Army does not need a permit and says it intends
to act on Tuesday.
Andrea Shue, NPR News.
Palestinian officials and witnesses say Israeli settlers set fire to cars and homes overnight
in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
A top Israeli politician is calling it Jewish terrorism.
And Piers Lauren Freire has more from Tel Aviv.
Israel shows at least a dozen cars on fire and racist graffiti with the word "revenge"
in Hebrew on Palestinian homes near Ramallah.
Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot calls it "Jewish terrorism" in every sense of
the word.
He blames extremist settlers who've set up illegal outposts in the area, and accuses
them of bringing the West Bank to the "brink of unchecked anarchy."
Eisenkot is leading coalition talks to oust Israel's far-right prime minister Benjamin
Netanyahu, who has extremist settlers in his cabinet.
Meanwhile, the United Nations says settler attacks on the Palestinian olive harvest hit
a record high this year.
The UN accuses Netanyahu's government of not only failing to stop them, but of actively
supporting them.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
After traveling for more than eight years, a joint European-Japanese mission has gone
into orbit around the planet Mercury.
Joe Palko reports the probe should provide scientists with a wealth of new information
about the innermost planet in the solar system.
Mercury is an intriguing planet.
It has an incredible number of scientific mysteries.
Anne Pomier at the Carnegie Institution is one of the scientists on the Bepi-Colombo
mission.
She says scientists have found evidence that there is ice at the poles of the planet, odd
for a planet so close to the sun.
It also has a larger metal core than expected.
The fact that this planet is shrinking also is another mystery.
Bepi-Colombo is scheduled to start answering scientific questions next spring.
But first, it will spend several months adjusting its orbit and checking out its instruments.
For NPR News, I'm Joe Palko.
At the weekend box office, The Hunger Games, Sunrise on the Reaping, debuted in the top
spot with an estimated $120 million in ticket sales.
The film focuses on the backstory of a beloved character, Hamish Abernathy.
This after 14 years and six movies.
This film is a sequel to Songbirds and Snakes, set 25 years before the original series.
In second place, the comic drama about the making of Rocky, called I Play Rocky, with
$9 million in its first weekend.
In third place, Johnny Depp's Ebenezer with $7 million.
The Paramount release has grossed $32 million domestically, $78 million globally.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: International climate talks in Turkey collapse over fossil fuel language, with Saudi Arabia rejecting it
Justice Department says Army will detonate five tons of lead azide in Iowa by Tuesday despite court pause
Israeli settlers set fire to Palestinian cars and homes near Ramallah; Gadi Eisenkot calls it Jewish terrorism
Joint European-Japanese BepiColombo probe enters orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opens at No. 1 with an estimated $120 million weekend
